examples.en: The way home is a steep hill road.

examples.ko: 아이들이 송아지를 끌고 꼬부라진 언덕길을 올라오고 있어요.
examples.en: The children are coming up the winding hill road, leading a calf.

examples.ko: 언덕길에서 자전거를 타면 내려갈 때 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: When you ride a bike on a hill road, you have to be careful going down.

examples.ko: 눈이 오면 언덕길이 미끄러워서 차가 못 다녀요.
examples.en: When it snows, the hill road is slippery and cars can't get through.
Every evening I take a slow walk along the hill road in my neighborhood.

examples.ko: 언덕길 끝에 작은 카페가 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small cafe at the end of the hill road.

explain: '오르막길', '내리막길'은 가는 방향에 초점이 있고, '언덕길'은 언덕에 나 있는 길 자체를 말해서 오르내리는 길 모두를 가리켜요. 그래서 올라갈 때도 내려갈 때도 '언덕길'이라고 할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: It was a steep hill road, so I pushed my bike up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가파르다'와 자주 함께 써요. 길이 얼마나 힘든지 말할 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 가파르다 to say how hard the road is.

phrases.en: I climbed the hill road slowly, catching my breath.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '을'을 붙여 올라가는 동작과 함께 쓴 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle 을 attaches it to the action of going up.

phrases.en: Be careful when you go down the hill road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '언덕길'은 내려가는 길에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 언덕길 can also be used for the way down.
phrases.en_equiv: to go down the hill road

explain_en: '오르막길' (uphill road) and '내리막길' (downhill road) focus on the direction you travel, while '언덕길' refers to the road on a hill itself, so it covers both going up and coming down.

t90.ax: The way home is a steep hill road.

examples.en: The kids are running up and down the stairs.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터가 고장 나서 오르락내리락 걸어 다녔어요.
examples.en: The elevator broke, so I walked up and down the stairs.
The stock price moved up and down all day.
The boat rocked up and down on the waves.
My fever kept going up and down, so I went to the hospital.
I walked up and down the mountain path and my legs hurt.

explain: 위로 올라갔다 아래로 내려갔다를 되풀이하는 모습을 나타내요. 계단이나 산길뿐 아니라 가격, 체온, 기분처럼 변하는 것에도 써요. 보통 '오르락내리락하다'로 동사처럼 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Vegetable prices go up and down these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계단뿐 아니라 값이 변하는 모습에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works not only for stairs but also for changing prices.

phrases.en: The child's temperature keeps going up and down, so I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸 상태가 안정되지 않고 변할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a body condition keeps changing and isn't stable.

phrases.en: My legs hurt from going up and down the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오르락내리락'보다 짧고 반복의 느낌이 약한 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter verb with less of a repetitive feel than 오르락내리락.

explain_en: It shows something repeatedly going up and then down. It is used not only for stairs and mountain paths but also for things that fluctuate, like prices, body temperature and mood. It is also very often used as the verb '오르락내리락하다'.

t90.ax: The boat rocked up and down on the waves.

en: to be sequestered; to be secluded; to be covert

examples.en: Avoid secluded alleys at night.
We wandered only through secluded back alleys.

examples.ko: 공원 안쪽은 으슥해서 혼자 가기 무서워요.
examples.en: The inside of the park is secluded, so it's scary to go alone.
A strange sound came from a hidden place.
After sunset, the forest path became gloomy and secluded.

examples.ko: 으슥한 길에서는 휴대폰을 보며 걷지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't walk looking at your phone on a secluded road.

explain: 사람이 별로 없고 구석져서 조용하며 조금 무서운 곳에 써요. '으슥한 골목/길/곳'처럼 뒤에 장소가 오는 경우가 많아요. 단순히 조용한 곳을 말하는 '한적하다'와 달리 불안한 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: Be careful in secluded places.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 없고 조금 무서운 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a place that is empty and a bit scary.

phrases.en: This road gets secluded after dark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 장소의 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form describing how a place feels.

phrases.en: This park is bright, so it isn't secluded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전하고 밝은 곳이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a place is safe and bright.

explain_en: It describes a place with few people, tucked away, quiet and a little scary. It is often followed by a place word, like '으슥한 골목/길/곳'. Unlike '한적하다', which just means quiet, it carries a feeling of unease.

examples.en: The electric pole fell backward because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 전봇대 옆에 쓰레기를 버리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not throw trash next to the electric pole.
I bumped my head on an electric pole while walking.
Flyers are plastered on every electric pole.
The meeting spot is in front of the blue electric pole.
Please park the car so it avoids the electric pole.

explain: '전신주'라는 말도 있지만 말할 때는 '전봇대'가 더 편하고 흔한 느낌이에요. 약속 장소를 알려 줄 때 '파란 전봇대 앞'처럼 길 표시로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: There is a utility pole standing by the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전봇대'와 같은 뜻이지만 글이나 공식적인 말에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '전봇대', but more common in writing and formal speech.

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the electric pole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 말할 때 길 표시로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it as a street landmark for a meeting place.

phrases.en: The bicycle hit the electric pole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어딘가에 세게 부딪혔을 때 '부딪히다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '부딪히다' when something hits against something.

explain_en: There is also the word '전신주', but '전봇대' feels more casual and natural in speech. People also use it as a landmark when giving directions, like '파란 전봇대 앞'.

t90.ax: Flyers are plastered on every electric pole.

examples.ko: 제트기가 큰 소리를 내며 하늘을 날았어요.
examples.en: A jet flew through the sky with a loud roar.
A jet is much faster than an ordinary plane.
I saw a private jet at the airport.

examples.ko: 이 제트기는 열 명만 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only ten people can ride this jet.
Since I was little, my dream was to be a jet pilot.
At the exhibition I climbed aboard an old jet.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '비행기'라고 하고, 제트기는 제트 엔진을 단 빠른 비행기를 따로 말할 때 써요. 싸우는 군용 비행기는 '전투기', 사람을 태우는 큰 비행기는 '여객기'예요.

phrases.en: I rode a jet plane for the first time yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제트기'만 말할 때보다 '타다'와 함께 쓰면 직접 경험한 일을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'to ride' lets you talk about a personal experience, not just the word 'jet'.

phrases.en: A jet is passing overhead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하늘에서 제트기가 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe a jet moving across the sky.

phrases.example: 제트기 소리가 너무 커서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: The jet noise was so loud that I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제트기'가 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 제트기와 관련된 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '제트기' modifies the next noun to name something related to jets.

explain_en: In daily life people just say 비행기, and 제트기 is used when specifically meaning a fast plane with a jet engine. A military fighting plane is a 전투기 and a large passenger plane is a 여객기.

en: to dash; to scoot; to scud

examples.en: The car speeds down the highway.
The horse raced across the wide field.
A motorcycle is speeding through the night streets.
The kids play, dashing across the playground.
It is dangerous to speed through and ignore the signal.

examples.ko: 기차가 어둠 속을 질주하는 모습이 멋졌어요.
examples.en: The sight of the train racing through the dark was great.

explain: '질주하다'는 '달리다'보다 속도가 크고 힘찬 느낌이 있어요. 차, 말, 기차 같은 것에 많이 쓰고 사람이 달릴 때는 '전력 질주하다'처럼 말해요. 가볍게 달릴 때는 '뛰다'나 '달리다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I sprinted at full speed to catch the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 힘껏 달릴 때 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The way to say a person runs flat out.

phrases.en: Be careful of speeding cars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 빠르게 달리는 모습을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to describe something racing.

phrases.en: Please don't speed down the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험하게 빨리 달리지 말라는 부탁이나 경고예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request or warning not to race around dangerously.

explain_en: 질주하다 feels faster and more forceful than the plain '달리다'. It is mostly used for cars, horses and trains, while for a person you say '전력 질주하다'. For light running '뛰다' or '달리다' is more natural.

examples.en: Two cars collided at the intersection.
Our opinions often clash.

examples.ko: 약속 시간이 서로 충돌해서 만날 수 없어요.
examples.en: Our appointment times conflict, so we can't meet.
There are many accidents where birds hit windows.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 크게 충돌한 뒤 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: After the two people had a big clash, they don't talk.

examples.ko: 일정이 충돌하지 않게 미리 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check ahead so the schedules don't conflict.

explain: '충돌하다'는 물건끼리 부딪힐 때도, 사람의 생각이나 일정이 안 맞을 때도 써요. 가볍게 몸이 닿을 때는 '부딪히다'를 쓰고 '충돌하다'는 크고 세게 부딪히는 느낌이에요. 일정이나 의견이 맞지 않을 때는 '겹치다', '맞지 않다'도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The two cars collided head-on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 앞에서 크게 부딪힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when objects hit each other head-on with force.

phrases.en: My meeting and my appointment clash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 일정이 같은 시간에 있어서 안 맞을 때 써요. 일상에서는 '겹치다'도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two schedules are at the same time. In daily talk '겹치다' is also used.

phrases.en: I almost collided with a bicycle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 부딪히지는 않았지만 아주 가까웠을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a crash almost happened but didn't.

explain_en: 충돌하다 is used both when objects crash and when opinions or schedules conflict. For light contact, 부딪히다 is used, while 충돌하다 feels bigger and harder. For schedules and opinions, 겹치다 or 맞지 않다 are also common.

examples.en: The stairs are narrow and steep, so you have to be careful.
The elevator was broken, so I went up by the stairs.
Kids are playing at the bottom of the stairs.
I came down those stairs slowly, one step at a time.
I left my umbrella at the end of the stairs.

examples.ko: 이 건물 층계는 폭이 넓어서 안전해요.
examples.en: The stairs in this building are wide, so they are safe.

explain: '계단'과 거의 같아서 바꿔 써도 돼요. 다만 '층계'는 조금 글 같은 느낌이 있어서, 대화에서는 '계단'이라고 말하는 사람이 많아요. '층계를 오르다/내려오다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I'm going down by the stairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고, 대화에서는 '층계'보다 '계단'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning; in conversation 'gyedan' is more common than 'cheunggye'.

phrases.en: If you go up the stairs, the office is on the right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위로 올라갈 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual verb pairing for going up the stairs.

phrases.en: I almost fell while coming down the stairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아래로 내려올 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual verb pairing for coming down the stairs.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '계단', so you can swap them. '층계' feels a bit more literary, and many people say '계단' in conversation. You say '층계를 오르다' (go up) or '층계를 내려오다' (come down).

t90.ax: I left my umbrella at the end of the stairs.

examples.en: I saw a big trailer truck on the highway.
The trailer truck is heading to the port with cargo.
My uncle drives a trailer truck.

examples.ko: 뒤에 트레일러가 붙은 차는 속도가 느려요.
examples.en: A vehicle with a trailer attached is slower.
The road was blocked because of a trailer accident.
We rented a camping trailer and travelled.

explain: 트레일러는 짐을 싣기 위해 트럭 뒤에 연결하는 큰 차량이에요. 한국에서는 짐을 싣는 큰 트럭을 말할 때 가장 많이 쓰고, 캠핑카처럼 뒤에 끌고 다니는 '캠핑 트레일러'도 있어요. 영화 예고편을 뜻하는 'trailer'는 한국어로 보통 '예고편'이라고 해서 구별해요.

phrases.en: My father is a trailer truck driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 트럭을 모는 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the job of driving a large truck.

phrases.en: I slept in a camping trailer on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 끌고 다니며 잘 수 있는 차량을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A towed vehicle you can sleep in.

phrases.en: A trailer truck passed slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짐을 싣는 큰 트럭을 조금 더 분명하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A clearer way to refer to the big cargo truck.

explain_en: A teureilleo is a large vehicle attached behind a truck to carry cargo. In Korea it mostly refers to big cargo trucks, though a 캠핑 트레일러 pulled behind a car also exists. A movie trailer is usually called 예고편, which keeps the two meanings apart.

t90.ax: My uncle drives a trailer truck.

examples.en: It is dangerous to cross a road without a traffic light.
He crossed the United States by bicycle.
The children cross the street with their hands raised.

examples.ko: 배로 바다를 횡단하는 데 열흘이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes ten days to cross the sea by ship.

examples.ko: 동물들이 도로를 횡단하지 못하게 울타리를 쳤어요.
examples.en: They put up a fence so animals cannot cross the road.

examples.ko: 신호가 바뀌면 횡단할 수 있으니까 조금만 기다려요.
examples.en: You can cross once the signal changes, so let's wait a moment.

explain: '건너다'보다 딱딱한 글 말투예요. '횡단보도', '대륙 횡단'처럼 굳은 말에서 자주 보여요. 길을 건널 때 일상에서는 '건너다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Cross slowly at the crosswalk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 사람이 건너는 곳을 말하고, 일상에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where people cross the street; very common in daily life.

phrases.en: He crossed the continent by train.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓은 땅을 가로질러 갈 때 쓰는 굳은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for traveling across a wide stretch of land.

phrases.en: Be careful when you cross the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '횡단하다'보다 '건너다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, 건너다 sounds much more natural.

explain_en: It is more formal than '건너다'. You see it in set words like '횡단보도' (crosswalk) and '대륙 횡단'. For crossing a street in daily life, '건너다' sounds much more natural.

t90.ax: He crossed the United States by bicycle.

en: to lose by a large margin

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 어제 경기에서 크게 대패했어요.
examples.en: Our team was badly beaten in yesterday's game.
The candidate who lost the election by a landslide apologized.

examples.ko: 상대 팀에게 대패해서 모두 말이 없었어요.
examples.en: We lost by a lot to the other team, so everyone was silent.
If you lose big in the first game, the mood sinks.

examples.ko: 이번에 대패한 이유를 같이 분석해 봤어요.
examples.en: We analyzed together why we lost so badly this time.
I got crushed by my friend in the game.

explain: 대패하다는 점수 차이가 크게 졌다는 느낌이라서 '크게 지다'와 거의 같아요. 반대는 '대승하다'이고, 아주 근소하게 지면 '석패하다'라고 해요. 같은 소리의 '대패'는 나무를 깎는 연장이라 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: Our team lost by a lot yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대패하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 대패하다, but easier and more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: The team that lost badly left the stadium quietly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 활용으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.en: In the end, we lost by a big margin.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 말다'가 붙어 안타까운 결과라는 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -고 말다 gives a feeling of regret about the result.

explain_en: 대패하다 feels like losing by a wide score gap, almost the same as 크게 지다. The opposite is 대승하다, and losing by a hair is 석패하다. The identically pronounced 대패 is a woodworking plane, a completely different word.

examples.en: The game ended in a tie.
When the score was tied, the crowd shouted.
Our team tied the score at the end.
The two people who were tied competed again.

examples.ko: 시험에서 두 학생이 동점이라 함께 일 등이 됐어요.
examples.en: Two students had the same score on the exam, so they tied for first place.
The equalizing goal came in the second half.

explain: 경기 중에 점수가 같아지는 순간과 점수가 같은 상태에 모두 써요. 경기가 같은 점수로 끝나면 '무승부'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The two teams tied in the second half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수가 같아지는 순간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the moment the scores become equal.

phrases.en: An equalizing goal was scored at the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수를 같게 만든 골을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the goal that makes the score even.

phrases.en: The game ended in a tie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝난 점수가 같을 때 쓰고, 같은 뜻으로 '무승부'도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the final score is equal; 무승부 means the same.

explain_en: It is used both for the moment the score becomes level and for the state of being level. A match that ends with equal scores is called a 무승부.

t90.ax: The game ended in a tie.

examples.en: The pitcher stepped onto the mound and threw the ball.
The pitcher on the mound looked nervous.
During the game, the manager walked to the mound.
The new pitcher held the mound.
The mound got wet because of the rain.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 마운드에서 내려오며 모자를 벗었어요.
examples.en: The player took off his cap as he came down from the mound.

explain: 타자가 서는 곳은 '타석', 투수가 서는 곳은 마운드예요. 투수가 바뀔 때 '마운드에 오르다', '마운드에서 내려오다'라고 말해요. 야구 중계에서 자주 들리는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The new pitcher went up to the mound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투수가 경기에 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a pitcher enters the game.

phrases.en: The pitcher was tired and came down from the mound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투수가 경기에서 빠질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a pitcher leaves the game.

phrases.en: That player stood on the mound for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투수로 던지는 자리에 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being in the pitcher's spot.

explain_en: The batter stands in the 타석, and the pitcher stands on the 마운드. When pitchers change, people say 마운드에 오르다 or 마운드에서 내려오다. You hear it often in baseball broadcasts.

examples.en: I bought a boomerang on my trip to Australia.
A boomerang flies far and then comes back.

examples.ko: 남을 욕한 말이 부메랑이 되어 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: The insults I said about others came back like a boomerang.

examples.ko: 아이는 종이로 부메랑을 접어서 친구에게 줬어요.
examples.en: The child folded a paper boomerang and gave it to a friend.

examples.ko: 그 정책은 결국 정부에 부메랑처럼 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: That policy ended up coming back at the government like a boomerang.

examples.ko: 부메랑에 적힌 이름을 보니 제 것이 아니었어요.
examples.en: The name written on the boomerang showed it was not mine.

explain: 부메랑이 되다, 부메랑으로 돌아오다는 내가 한 말이나 행동이 결국 나에게 되돌아온다는 비유로 자주 써요. 뉴스에서는 '부메랑 효과'라고도 해요. 한자어 '자업자득'보다 부드럽고 일상적인 말이에요.

phrases.example: 남을 속인 일이 부메랑이 되어 돌아왔어요.
phrases.en: to come back like a boomerang
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 한 행동의 결과가 나쁜 쪽으로 나에게 돌아온다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for the bad results of your own actions coming back to you.
phrases.en_equiv: come back to bite you; backfire

explain_en: 부메랑이 되다 and 부메랑으로 돌아오다 are common figures of speech for your own words or actions coming back to you. The news also uses 부메랑 효과. It is softer and more everyday than the Sino-Korean 자업자득.
